tickets.title: Restore ingestion completion and safe resume
tickets.what: An operator can ingest bounded input and resume a completed capture without another collector call or losing prior run history.
tickets.scope: Repair the existing evidence-save completion contract and its caller compatibility only; introduce no task queue or unrelated refactor.
criteria: The evidence-save operation accepts an explicit final-input marker and a backward-compatible default for callers that do not provide it.
Observation persistence, checkpoint advancement, and final-input marking commit together, including caller-owned transactions.
At the request/record limit, a saved final capture resumes into canonical processing without another collector call; an interrupted nonfinal capture remains resumable.
Existing run migration and retained/transient replay scenarios preserve IDs and prior observations.
The shared repository check is green with the test database available; the current undefined-completion and unexpected-argument failures are resolved.

tickets.title: Publish and inspect permitted ingested support
tickets.what: An operator can publish a bounded selection of already-ingested evidence and reopen a knowledge-publication detail page with exact usable support.
tickets.scope: Deliver publication by identity for a bounded source-only selection and supported existing caption interpretations; no general search, background tasks, embeddings, or new ontology.
criteria: A trusted operation publishes validated observation/derivation/assertion references with method versions, source times, publication time, coverage, and actual producer.
A source-backed account can be published with unknown profile/interpretation attributes; unsupported claims and un-ingested references cannot be published as facts.
A local publication detail surface reopens the committed selection and exact support after restart; partially prepared support is never visible as a committed publication.
Identical concurrent publication requests return one logical publication; changed payload under the same request identity conflicts.
Process/display/retention policy, commit-time withdrawal, superseded support, and later redaction or copy purge retain the existing evidence-owner contract.
Adding a new publication never mutates imported evidence-set membership or previously pinned support; existing pilot reads and explicit development-only synthetic visibility remain compatible.

tickets.title: Search current knowledge and pin result support
tickets.what: A marketer can search published knowledge, inspect coverage and freshness, and reopen the exact support selection behind a result.
tickets.scope: Use bounded text/subject/platform/time filters and a stable support manifest; defer semantic/vector search and graph navigation.
criteria: A public query and local knowledge-search surface search only committed, permitted publications and expose source references, relevant dates, methods, unknowns, and coverage.
Search distinguishes age-based freshness from permission/derivation health and does not count ingestion/publication time as a new capture.
A consequential query result can pin the actual observation/assertion/interpretation membership and versions used, rather than only storing the query.
A later publication can appear in a new query while an earlier pinned result retains exact membership and unavailable/superseded support indicators.
Queries and reopened results honor workspace and purpose boundaries, exclude synthetic inputs unless explicitly selected for development, and do not leak pending raw responses or denied text.
Default integration tests use real public readers and PostgreSQL, including source-only accounts, empty scope, newer publications, and withdrawal.

tickets.title: Run one authorized offline acquisition task
tickets.what: A marketer can submit one bounded offline acquisition for an existing campaign, receive a task identity immediately, and inspect its ingestion and publication outcome.
tickets.scope: One server-authorized campaign origin, one offline route, and one bounded worker entry point; reject unsupported origins and keep live execution disabled.
criteria: Trusted campaign context establishes task origin and immutable scope/limits; arbitrary actor/origin fields cannot create schedule or assistant authority.
Submission persists actor, campaign basis, scope version, request identity, limits, and initial status before returning acknowledgment; it does not synchronously fetch.
A bounded worker uses the existing ingestion runner and publication operation, records its attempt/run links, and exposes a local task-detail surface after restart.
Queue acceptance, collection, ingestion, publication, failure, and no-usable-update meanings are distinguishable; raw fetch success alone never means a successful KB update.
Identical submission retries return the same task; changed scope under the same identity conflicts; foreign workspaces and forged origins dispatch no work.
No real source/model calls are possible in this slice; empty or unchanged inputs do not create fictitious update claims.

tickets.title: Approve an exact assistant enrichment proposal
tickets.what: A marketer can review a saved enrichment proposal, explicitly approve that exact scope, and submit an attributable offline task.
tickets.scope: A direct local proposal/review/approval interaction using a supplied proposal; defer conversational generation of the proposal.
criteria: A proposal revision visibly states purpose, refresh/fill/expansion intent, subject/search scope, and workspace before any acquisition task is submitted.
Only an attributable human action approves the exact proposal revision and scope; generated text or submitted actor kind is not approval.
Approval and retry-safe task submission bind one logical task to that approval; an identical retry cannot mint another task.
Changed or materially broader scope, missing approval, foreign workspace, and forged campaign/schedule origin are rejected before dispatch.
Approved on-demand scope may go beyond registered scheduled keywords while still honoring task limits.
The local approval and resulting task pages reopen exact attribution and scope after restart with existing form/Origin/CSRF protection.

tickets.title: Recover interrupted tasks and expose partial outcomes
tickets.what: An operator can resume an interrupted task and see which knowledge became usable, which phase failed, and what remains incomplete.
tickets.scope: Single-worker recovery and the outcome matrix for one bounded route; worker competition and notification delivery are separate tickets.
criteria: Persist phase/attempt progress so restarting after evidence, canonical, or publication commit reuses committed effects rather than starting a fresh acquisition.
Tasks expose usable update, partial update, no usable update, and failure with sanitized phase-specific reasons and actual coverage.
One valid and one failed input preserve the valid committed publication while reporting the failed remainder; unpublished material stays unavailable to KB queries.
Unchanged already-published evidence and empty eligible results are reported without inventing a newly usable update or market-absence claim.
Pending provider state is representable as waiting/resumable progress; an ambiguous chargeable operation cannot be blindly reissued.
Fault-injection tests at public worker boundaries verify restart behavior and stable support/attempt identities using real persistence.

tickets.title: Coordinate competing workers without duplicate effects
tickets.what: Multiple workers can process the durable task frontier while an interrupted or stale worker cannot duplicate or overwrite completed work.
tickets.scope: Claim, handoff, and stale-worker protection for the established task lifecycle; do not introduce a distributed broker or general workflow engine.
criteria: Competing public worker claims grant one active execution authority for the same task phase and expose queued/running/recoverable state accurately.
Worker handoff after interruption uses committed progress and cannot create duplicate observations, publications, or logical task outcomes.
A worker that lost authority cannot commit stale results over a successor's progress.
Independent tasks can progress without one task's claim serializing the entire workspace.
Real competing connections/processes exercise claim races, lost acknowledgment, and recovery; sequential helper calls are not accepted as concurrency proof.
The visible task history records bounded attempts and recovery without exposing payloads or secrets.

tickets.title: Deliver durable task completion notifications
tickets.what: A marketer can reopen an in-application inbox and follow task completion messages to the actual usable update, partial result, or failure.
tickets.scope: Local durable inbox and task completion delivery only; defer campaign regeneration actions and external message transports.
criteria: Task completion and its logical notification are persisted consistently so interruption after a committed outcome cannot permanently hide completion.
Usable, partial, no-update, and failed outcomes have distinct concise messages with task/publication links and actual coverage.
Repeated delivery/resumption references one logical event; it does not invent multiple completed updates.
Inbox and task/publication navigation survive application restart and remain workspace scoped.
Notification text and source-dependent links apply current display/retention policy; unavailable support does not leak copied wording.
No email, Slack, push transport, or unrequested external messaging is introduced.

tickets.title: Show attributable actual costs and forecasts
tickets.what: An operator can inspect a task's measured usage and derived charges separately from forecasts and outstanding commitments.
tickets.scope: One configured synthetic metered service and one forecast-only scope, through a public usage operation and local cost detail; no real paid calls or ceiling enforcement yet.
criteria: Persist explicit metered/forecast-only classification, currency, period, service/provider, attributable task/attempt or operation, units, rate version, and measurement provenance/time.

Measured usage or charges produce derivable actual spending with auditable rate inputs; estimates and forecasts do not masquerade as actuals, and simulated measurements are labeled synthetic rather than commercial charges.
Repeated measurement identity reconciles once and conflicting reuse is visible rather than silently overwriting accounting history.
The cost surface distinguishes actuals, commitments, forecasts, unknown coverage, and meter failure; unknown cost is not zero.
Model operations without an acquisition task can receive an equivalent attributable operation identity.
Public-interface integration tests use simulated units/rates and prove forecast-only scopes never claim enforced monetary control.

tickets.title: Enforce shared monetary admission before work
tickets.what: An operator can configure a metered ceiling and see competing chargeable operations admitted or refused before their simulated external calls.
tickets.scope: Coordinated bounded commitments and ceiling admission for the existing synthetic cost scope; delayed billing and uncertain outcomes follow separately.
criteria: Configured ceilings have explicit currency, accounting period, and cost scope; admissions consider actual spend plus outstanding bounded commitments.
Competing workers and public operation adapters share one authoritative admission decision and cannot exceed available bounded commitments through races.
Refused or paused work makes no additional chargeable call and exposes its allowance/blocked reason in task or operation status.
Task approval, scheduled authorization, and automatic shortlist saving cannot bypass monetary admission.
Forecast-only scopes remain forecast-only and retain request/record/byte bounds independently.
Tests use genuinely competing admissions and a counted fake transport, including exact allowance, exhausted allowance, and missing required control.

tickets.title: Reconcile delayed charges and failed meters
tickets.what: An operator can reconcile delayed or uncertain charges after retries and restarts without double-counting or accidentally reopening an exhausted allowance.
tickets.scope: The established meter/commitment workflow, including late actuals and explicit control failure; do not add more providers.
criteria: Late provider measurements replace or settle the correct outstanding commitment idempotently while preserving the measurement/rate audit trail.
Ambiguous remote-call outcomes retain an explicit unresolved commitment until reconciled or handled by a recorded bounded policy.
Retry and restart cannot double-charge accounting or release an unresolved operation as free work.
An unavailable expected meter pauses/refuses further work in that scope and presents a visible control failure rather than silently switching to forecasts.
Known charge bounds, billing lag, and strict-enforcement limitations are displayed; unbounded/delayed charges never imply guaranteed zero overshoot.
Integration tests cover late success/failure, replayed billing, conflicting measurements, restart, and meter recovery through public operations.

tickets.title: Save visible executable campaign criteria
tickets.what: A marketer can save and inspect a versioned executable criteria/ranking profile for a campaign using structured inputs.
tickets.scope: Extend the existing brief workflow with a visible structured profile; no LLM interpretation, current-KB retrieval, or new ranking algorithm.
criteria: Campaign editing records stable criteria identifiers, requirements/preferences/exclusions, explicit unknown handling, and the applicable ranking/coverage profile versions.
The saved interpretation is visible alongside the marketer's original input and pins the exact brief revision.
Stale edits conflict through expected-version checks; changed input creates an attributable successor rather than rewriting history.
Unknown audience, fees, availability, and sales assumptions remain unknown unless supported; structured labels cannot assert source facts.
Existing human campaign, measurement-plan, decision-note, and protected form behavior remains compatible.
A public-store and HTTP journey can create, revise, restart, and inspect the exact profile.

tickets.title: Interpret natural-language criteria with one metered model
tickets.what: A marketer can turn natural-language campaign criteria into a visible, versioned executable interpretation using one explicitly configured model route.
tickets.scope: One provider transport and one bounded criteria-interpretation journey; default tests simulate transport and live enablement requires explicit configuration.
criteria: Natural-language input produces a contract-validated interpretation with requirements, preferences, exclusions, unknown handling, method/model versions, and original-input linkage.
The executable interpretation is visible before it is used for assessment and remains pinned to the exact brief/profile revision.
Malformed or unsupported generated criteria fail visibly; source/model text cannot grant task authority, broaden approval, or override constraints.
The configured model route records attributable usage, obtains cost admission before calls, reconciles outcomes, and respects request/output bounds.
Missing key, model configuration, rate classification, or admission yields a visible unavailable/blocked capability rather than an unbounded call or invented interpretation.

Verify the selected provider's current primary contract during implementation; use simulated success/failure/authority-forgery responses in default integration tests and record any separately authorized live receipt.

tickets.title: Compare eligible accounts from current knowledge
tickets.what: A marketer can compare current-KB accounts against a campaign's recorded criteria with exact supporting evidence and explicit unknowns.
tickets.scope: Reuse the existing deterministic caption criteria for a bounded KB candidate set; no automatic shortlist saves or LLM assessment yet.
criteria: Candidates come only from current permitted KB support within the campaign scope and carry the exact retrieved support manifest/profile/brief versions.
Stable account identity plus one permitted ingested supporting observation is sufficient for eligibility; incomplete profiles remain explicit.
Handle-only or un-ingested references may appear as discovery seeds/gaps but never as supported comparison candidates.
Required exclusions and unknown policies affect the displayed assessment; caption language/PR markers do not imply audience geography or contracts.
Comparison details expose support, source dates, freshness, gaps, empty results, and actual method without pretending to be an LLM rank.
Preparation and reopen tests cover withdrawal races, newer publications, source namespaces, and immutable historical comparisons.

tickets.title: Automatically save an attributed ordered shortlist
tickets.what: A campaign's supported deterministic recommendation is saved automatically as an ordered shortlist revision that can be reopened without a human-review step.
tickets.scope: Implement automated save authority and ordered persistence using the existing deterministic assessment; semantic LLM ranking and optional human curation are separate.
criteria: A recommendation operation automatically persists the actual automation producer, exact brief/profile/method, candidate order, rationale, gaps, and pinned support.
An empty eligible result is saved explicitly; no un-ingested account or fabricated evidence is inserted to avoid an empty shortlist.
Saving requires no human approval/review/confirmation and never fabricates human authorship or endorsement.
Identical requests reopen the original saved revision without reassessment; changed payload under a request identity and stale revision updates conflict.
Existing human shortlist records and their statuses/attribution survive schema upgrade and restart unchanged.
Saved explanations enforce current policy and retention withdrawal while permitted historical membership and producer attribution remain pinned.

tickets.title: Rank campaign candidates with supported LLM assessment
tickets.what: A marketer receives an automatically saved campaign shortlist ordered by validated LLM assessment of a bounded current-KB candidate set.
tickets.scope: One configured method/profile and bounded candidate batch using the established model transport; no discovery, model-driven tool loop, or new provider.
criteria: Deterministic eligibility/requirements run before the bounded LLM assessment; incomplete supported accounts remain eligible subject to explicit unknown handling.
The saved result records actual assessed support, candidate ordering, reasons/gaps, model/method/profile versions, and automated producer.
Generated judgments may cite only permitted support belonging to assessed candidates; invented accounts, unsupported reasons, and malformed output fail or remain explicitly unassessed.
Source content cannot change tools, task origin, approvals, scope, or spending; model failure cannot be mislabeled as successful LLM ranking.
All model calls use the existing metering/admission contract; retrying a completed recommendation reopens its saved revision without another model call.
Public recommendation and UI tests cover missing attributes, constrained criteria, empty candidates, unsupported output, withdrawal, and restart.

tickets.title: Curate generated shortlists without rewriting history
tickets.what: A marketer can optionally curate a generated shortlist and save an attributable successor while preserving the original automated recommendation.
tickets.scope: Extend existing human selection/history forms to generated ordered revisions; do not add a mandatory review gate.
criteria: Human curation can select/reorder accounts and record supported reasons/acknowledged unknowns as a new revision with actual human attribution.
The original automated rank, producer, support, and lack of human review remain unchanged.
Stale heads and conflicting retry identities fail visibly; an identical human save retries safely.
Current source-policy restrictions and inherited support apply to copied human reasons and submitted forms.
Existing historical human selections, confirmations, plans, and notes reopen with their original meaning after upgrade.
HTTP and public-store tests demonstrate optional curation and history without requiring a curation action before automated saving.

tickets.title: Execute bounded offline keyword discovery
tickets.what: An authorized task can search a scoped offline discovery route, ingest newly found records, and expose the resulting published KB updates.
tickets.scope: One deterministic query-discovery route and capability contract; no real provider, automatic fallback, scheduler, or supplemental retrieval.
criteria: Discovery accepts explicit query/subject/time scope and bounded limits rather than pretending a supplied-profile collector performs keyword search.
Configured capability and task authority are checked before dispatch; unsupported query routes expose an accurate unavailable reason.
A bounded offline discovery response flows through normal ingestion/publication and appears in current knowledge with query/route/selection lineage.
Results record actual capture times, coverage, missing fields, source identities, and prioritization/method context without inventing complete market coverage.
Empty, unchanged, partially valid, and failed results preserve the existing truthful task outcome meanings.
The public task/UI journey uses deterministic source-shaped fixtures and verifies no live calls, no duplicate publication benefit, and permitted support.

tickets.title: Queue discovery when campaign coverage is insufficient
tickets.what: A marketer receives the current supported shortlist immediately while inadequate quantity, relevance, or freshness automatically queues bounded campaign discovery.
tickets.scope: One visible versioned coverage policy and its automatic task submission; do not regenerate or replace saved results.
criteria: Assess actual candidate quantity, relevance, and freshness against a recorded coverage profile and show the reasons/coverage with the saved result.
Insufficient coverage establishes campaign task authority server-side and submits an associated bounded discovery task without asking for assistant approval.
Repeated coverage evaluation does not duplicate the same logical discovery request; forged campaign origin still cannot bypass assistant approval.
The current supported shortlist remains available, including an empty result, while the task is queued/running.
Source/cost admission failure is shown as blocked/refused enrichment without losing or fabricating the recommendation.
Public application tests demonstrate sufficient, thin, stale, empty, repeated, and refused cases through shortlist and task views.

tickets.title: Offer explicit regeneration after campaign updates
tickets.what: A campaign discovery completion notification offers regeneration, and only a marketer's explicit action creates a newly assessed saved shortlist revision.
tickets.scope: Reuse the configured recommendation method and completion inbox; no silent rerank, automatic replacement, or new ranking method.
criteria: Usable or partial published updates link the campaign notification to exact task/publication outcomes and an explicit regeneration action.
No-update/failure messages do not imply new evidence is available for a better recommendation.
Before the action, the saved shortlist's membership, order, methods, and support remain unchanged.
The explicit action uses the current campaign context, performs the configured assessment, and automatically saves an attributed successor under concurrency checks.
Duplicate action submission returns the same successor; a changed brief or stale version produces a visible conflict/recovery path.
A restart-capable HTTP journey verifies notification, no background mutation, regeneration, and both historical revisions.

tickets.title: Schedule offline discovery for registered keywords
tickets.what: An operator can register scheduled keywords and inspect due offline discovery tasks created under the schedule's recorded authority.
tickets.scope: Keyword configuration and durable due-task creation/execution through the offline discovery route; keep live schedule activation disabled.
criteria: A local configuration surface and public operation allow up to ten registered scheduled keywords per workspace, independently from monitoring topics.
Schedule records include configuration version and explicit day/timezone/cadence context; scheduled tasks retain their actual schedule/keyword authority.
A due tick creates bounded offline tasks once per logical scheduled occurrence and exposes status through the existing task surface.
Assistant/client input cannot choose schedule origin to bypass approval, and on-demand approved scope is not restricted to the registered list.
Restarts and concurrent due ticks do not create duplicate occurrences or reset recorded schedule history.
The UI labels the route offline and the daily target as a configurable admission allowance rather than measured throughput or per-keyword yield.

tickets.title: Enforce the shared daily unique-post allowance
tickets.what: Scheduled discovery admits at most the configured daily total of unique eligible new posts across all keywords and competing workers.
tickets.scope: Atomic new-post admission at the established scheduled ingestion boundary; do not treat request counts, refreshes, or costs as the same allowance.
criteria: The initial configurable total is fifty unique eligible new posts per workspace/day across all registered keywords, not fifty per keyword.

Overlapping query results and competing tasks cannot admit the same eligible new post twice or collectively exceed the day's allowance; invalid/denied records do not count as successful new-post admission, and failed admission/ingestion releases or reconciles reservations safely.
Known-record refreshes remain distinct from new-post admission and cannot be disguised as additional new eligible posts.
Restarts, keyword edits, and configuration revisions preserve consumption under the recorded accounting-day/timezone boundary.
Task and schedule views show used/remaining allowance, deduplication, limits, and legitimate fewer-record outcomes without promising a fill target.
Real competing public operations test overlapping identities, exhausted allowance, day rollover, and configuration changes without paid I/O.

tickets.title: Avoid redundant discovery while preserving refresh history
tickets.what: An operator can see unnecessary repeated retrieval skipped while legitimate stale-record refreshes and new observations retain their provenance.
tickets.scope: One discovery route's query/retrieval history and explicit freshness/processing policy; no global cross-provider identity merge or automatic fallback.
criteria: Persist prior query/retrieval scope, source identity, capture time, failures, usable publication, and method/version context needed for an explicit avoidance decision.
Repeated unchanged work within the configured freshness policy can be skipped with an inspectable reason rather than re-fetched or re-published as a new update.
Stale captures, changed source observations, required mapper revisions, and recoverable failed work remain eligible for appropriate new processing.
Unknown or unavailable freshness stays explicit; import/publication time cannot make old captures current.
Source namespaces, metric definitions, conflict history, and old result pins remain separate across refresh and deduplication.
Public task/KB tests count simulated retrievals and verify skip/refresh/failure behavior and historical support after restart.

tickets.title: Enable one verified live on-demand discovery route
tickets.what: An authorized on-demand task can use one explicitly configured live TikTok query-discovery route and report the actual usable KB update and attributable cost.
tickets.scope: One provider, platform, and query type; schedules remain offline until their separate activation ticket, and no automatic provider fallback is added.
criteria: Select and verify one permitted discovery-capable route against current primary documentation and bounded responses during implementation; existing supplied-profile/oEmbed success is insufficient.
Use the established query task, worker coordination, retrieval avoidance, normal ingestion/publication, coverage, and source-policy contracts.
Before every chargeable call, enforce configured admission and bounded commitments; account for actual known units/charges and expose forecast-only or delayed portions.
Pending/ambiguous provider work resumes or reconciles without a blind paid retry; source/schema/identity conflicts yield accurate partial/failure outcomes.
Missing credentials, source-use policy, required route/cost configuration, or explicit live-operation authorization is an unmet external prerequisite, never an invented readiness pass.

Default tests remain simulated. A separately authorized bounded live receipt records requests, returned/usable records, capture times, missingness, and derivable charges without secrets; preserve source-specific identities and semantics.

tickets.title: Activate live scheduled discovery within daily bounds
tickets.what: An operator can enable a verified live route for scheduled keyword discovery while the shared daily new-post allowance and spending controls remain enforced.
tickets.scope: Connect the proven live route to the existing scheduler and allowance; no new provider, query type, or scheduling engine.
criteria: Explicit route/schedule configuration enables live scheduled tasks under recorded schedule authority; an offline schedule never becomes live silently.
All keywords share the configured unique-new-post/day allowance and normal freshness/avoidance policy.
Every attempted provider operation uses shared spending admission, route limits, and recovery; exhausted daily or monetary allowance stops further relevant work visibly.
Scheduled outcomes distinguish fetched records, admitted new posts, usable publications, unchanged records, and partial/no-update results.
Restart/concurrent schedule tests with simulated live transport verify actual call counts and no bypass via origin or configuration changes.
Live execution still requires the established external configuration/authorization; no additional paid validation is silently authorized.

tickets.title: Supplement one valuable missing field and stop by value
tickets.what: A discovery task can selectively retrieve one configured missing field from an existing supplementary route and explain why it continued or stopped.
tickets.scope: One supported missing-field case and one supplementary route; no general autonomous research loop or arbitrary route switching.
criteria: An explicit selection policy considers missingness, freshness, permission, capability, expected information value, and cost before requesting supplementation.
Only the valuable in-scope record/field is fetched using parent task authority, remaining request/byte/record limits, and shared spending admission.
Supplementary observations retain their own source namespace, metric meaning, capture times, and provenance; conflicting support is not silently merged.
Unchanged evidence, unavailable capability, insufficient value, exhausted limits, source failure, or denied cost admission each produces an inspectable stopping reason.
Reference-only oEmbed responses cannot be turned into retained creator/account facts or comparison-grade evidence.
The task detail and resulting KB view show the actual new support/unknowns; counted fake transports verify no extra call after a stop condition.

tickets.title: Answer free-form questions from permitted knowledge
tickets.what: A marketer can ask a free-form KB question and receive an answer with inspectable support, dates, uncertainty, and explicit missing information.
tickets.scope: Bounded knowledge retrieval and one model-backed answer journey using the established metered transport; no enrichment submission or external search tools.
criteria: A local question/answer surface delegates to current permitted KB queries and records the actual support manifest and model/method context used.
Supported claims cite relevant permitted observations/interpretations and dates; missing, stale, ambiguous, or unsupported information remains explicit.
Reading existing knowledge requires no enrichment approval; no provider acquisition results or pending publication can support an answer.
Generated output is validated against the allowed support; evidence text cannot authorize tools, broaden scope, change actor authority, or override spending.
Model calls use shared cost admission and attributable usage; missing model/configuration or invalid output is a visible limitation/failure.
Reopened answer/support views and later questions respect current source policy and new publications without rewriting historical support.

tickets.title: Turn assistant knowledge gaps into approved enrichment
tickets.what: A marketer can turn an unanswered or stale assistant question into a scoped proposal, approve it, follow the task, and use published updates in a later query.
tickets.scope: Compose the existing question, proposal/approval, task, and notification operations into one assistant journey; do not add new acquisition or model providers.
criteria: An assistant knowledge gap can produce a visible proposal for refresh, attribute fill, or bounded subject expansion with an identifiable exact scope.
The assistant cannot submit before actual human approval and cannot convert a model-generated statement, forged origin, or changed scope into authority.
Approved scope may exceed scheduled keywords; material expansion requires corresponding new approval and still respects cost/source/task bounds.
After approval the interaction returns a task acknowledgment/status and later the durable actual completion/partial/failure notification.
Newly fetched information is never returned as a KB answer before ingestion/publication; a later explicit query can use usable publications.
HTTP/public-operation tests cover successful update, publication failure, broadened proposal, foreign actor, repeated approval, and source withdrawal.

tickets.title: Collect bounded recent X evidence offline
tickets.what: An operator can configure an X monitoring topic, run a bounded offline collection window, and inspect retained recent observations independently of the full KB.
tickets.scope: One deterministic recent-X route, one topic/window collection journey, and retention/policy-aware timeline; no alerts, live provider, or full KB ingestion.
criteria: Persist monitoring topic configuration separately from scheduled keywords with explicit cadence/window, bounded collection, source policy, and retention settings.
A public bounded poll entry point retains recent observations with stable source references/identities, capture/publication times, window coverage, and acquisition context.
The topic/window/timeline surface reopens observations after restart without creating campaigns or requiring knowledge publications for every post.
Retries do not duplicate a logical window's observations; missing fields and incomplete coverage remain visible.
Process/display/retention permissions, expiry, and withdrawal govern retained monitoring copies and their detail views.
Offline integration tests prohibit external I/O and prove existing frozen-snapshot investigations keep their original independent behavior.

tickets.title: Detect quantitative X anomalies with retained alerts
tickets.what: A marketer receives an inspectable alert when a configured quantitative method finds a justified X volume or engagement anomaly.
tickets.scope: One configured quantitative method and comparable baseline/window pair, with retained alert history and local inbox delivery; no semantic detection or external investigation.
criteria: Record explicit detection/baseline windows, sampling and metric comparability, method/version, significance configuration, coverage, and necessary evidence.
A supported significant change creates a retained alert and concise durable notification with evidence and uncertainty.
Absent/incomparable baselines or insufficient coverage cannot produce an unsupported numerical spike claim and are visible as assessment limitations.
Alert detail/history survive restart and reflect current policy, expiry, and unavailable support without retaining denied copied wording.
Detection requires no full KB publication for all recent observations and cannot create campaigns, expand topic scope, or launch external searches.
Public polling/detection/inbox tests use controlled windows for real anomaly, no anomaly, missing baseline, changed sampling, retries, and withdrawal.

tickets.title: Detect supported semantic X anomalies
tickets.what: A marketer can inspect semantic-shift or controversy alerts supported by retained recent X evidence and a versioned assessment method.
tickets.scope: One bounded semantic method using the established metered model transport and alert contract; no external-search agent or new provider.
criteria: Semantic assessment records method/model versions, selected windows/comparison context where applicable, actual recent support, uncertainty, and coverage limits.
A significant supported semantic finding produces an alert and local notification distinguishable from a quantitative measurement.
Malformed, unsupported, or source-injected generated output cannot invent support, approve work, expand monitoring topics, or call external research.
Missing comparison context cannot be hidden behind a confident change claim; method limitations remain inspectable.
Model calls obtain shared cost admission and usage attribution; default tests use controlled simulated responses and counted I/O.
Alert copies and reopened support honor source permissions/retention withdrawal, with exact historical method/window references preserved.

tickets.title: Explain X alerts using existing KB context only
tickets.what: A marketer can open an X alert and see relevant existing KB context separately from the recent evidence that triggered detection.
tickets.scope: Bounded existing-KB context lookup and explanation for the shared alert contract; no new external searches or automatic campaign initiation.
criteria: The investigation reads only committed permitted KB knowledge available to its bounded query and pins the exact supporting context selected.
Alert detail distinguishes recent monitoring evidence, existing KB context, and derived explanation with dates, coverage, and uncertainty.
An investigation has no authority/capability to submit enrichment, forge scheduled collection, broaden configured topics, or create campaigns.
Missing KB context yields an explicit gap rather than external fallback or invented facts.
Current policy and newer publications do not substitute new evidence into a saved alert's context; denied dependencies redact copied explanations.
Public integration tests count external/model acquisition transports as forbidden and verify the same behavior for any supported alert method.

tickets.title: Promote selected monitoring evidence into knowledge
tickets.what: An operator can deliberately promote selected permitted recent X observations through normal ingestion and publication, with traceable origins.
tickets.scope: One local selected-observation promotion path; do not fetch new data or publish the whole feed automatically.
criteria: A trusted explicit selection creates normal source observations/canonical mappings where supported and usable knowledge publications with links back to the monitoring inputs.
Promotion preserves source policy, capture times, native identities/namespaces, metric semantics, mapper versions, and unknown identity fields.
Retrying the same promotion does not duplicate canonical effects or logical publications.
No additional provider request or campaign is created; unselected observations remain solely in the bounded monitoring evidence path.
Monitoring and KB/alert copies honor their applicable retention, expiry, and withdrawal dependencies without using promotion to bypass denied support.
A local selection/result surface and public integration tests verify lineage, repeat promotion, partial invalid records, and policy changes.

tickets.title: Enable one verified live recent-X route
tickets.what: An operator can enable one configured live recent-X collection route for monitoring topics and inspect bounded recent windows without full KB ingestion.
tickets.scope: One provider and recent-post query type wired to existing topic/window collection; no new anomaly method or external follow-up research.
criteria: Verify the selected route's current primary contract, permitted use, identities, pagination, limits, and bounded response shape during implementation.
Configured periodic polling uses coordinated worker execution and creates exact recent windows under topic authority, independently of KB publication.
Source limits, request/byte/record bounds, shared spending admission, usage/reconciliation, and retention apply before and after each call.
Pending/ambiguous outcomes and concurrent due polls do not blindly repeat chargeable work or duplicate logical windows.
Missing credentials/policy/cost configuration or explicit live authorization remains an external prerequisite; never invent a successful readiness receipt.
Default tests simulate transport. Any separately authorized bounded live receipt records actual attempts, timestamps, missingness, coverage and derivable costs without secrets.

tickets.title: Search graph entities and inspect supported neighbors
tickets.what: A marketer can search permitted KB entities and inspect their immediate relationships and source evidence in a graph-oriented view.
tickets.scope: One-hop entity/relationship projection over existing governed knowledge; no graph database, inferred Creator merging, or multi-hop exploration yet.
criteria: A public projection and local graph surface search/filter supported entities and show a selected entity's immediate permitted relationships.
Relationship details distinguish observed, derived, and human bases and link to relevant source support/methods/dates.
Uncorroborated matching handles cannot create cross-platform Creator associations.
Process/display and withdrawal rules govern both graph labels and evidence details, including relationships whose support becomes unavailable.
Projection work uses owning public read interfaces and does not become another raw-fact store.
Public/HTTP tests cover empty search, bounded neighbors, differing relationship bases, foreign workspace, and denied support without leaks.

tickets.title: Traverse and filter governed graph relationships
tickets.what: A marketer can traverse multiple permitted graph relationships and narrow the view without losing relationship basis or evidence.
tickets.scope: Bounded multi-hop navigation, filters, and entity detail expansion on the existing projection; no new ontology or datastore.
criteria: Graph navigation supports explicit bounded traversal and filters for applicable entity/relationship/source context, with visible truncation or empty results.
Each traversed relationship remains inspectable with its observed/derived/human basis and supporting evidence.
Cycles, hidden nodes, and large neighborhoods cannot cause unbounded expansion or reveal denied labels through counts/details.
Policy changes invalidate/redact affected displayed detail without reconstructing withdrawn source wording.
Navigation and back/reopen behavior retain meaningful selection/filter context without implying historical graph membership is an immutable campaign decision.
HTTP/public-read tests exercise multi-hop navigation, cycles, bounded results, filters, and policy changes.

tickets.title: Trace tasks through publications and attributable costs
tickets.what: An operator can trace an acquisition task through attempts, runs, observations, transformations, publications, failures, and attributable usage in one lineage view.
tickets.scope: Read-only task-to-publication lineage using public owners and existing status/cost records; no generic observability platform or graph-explorer dependency.
criteria: A public lineage read and local view connect the actual task/authority to bounded attempts, ingestion runs, observations, derivation/method versions, and resulting publications.
The view makes queue acceptance, source success, partial ingestion, publication failure, no update, and usable completion visibly distinct.
Cost context links actuals, commitments, forecasts, meter provenance/lag, and unknown coverage where available without claiming unenforced ceilings.
Support/source excerpts pass current permissions, retention, and workspace checks; no credential or unrestricted provider payload appears in detail or errors.
Restart and recovery histories preserve links rather than inventing a successful continuous pipeline.
Public/HTTP tests exercise a successful trace, partial failure, resumed attempt, denied support, and cost attribution through real stores.

tickets.title: Prepare and validate operational quality-review packets
tickets.what: A reviewer can obtain and record attributable language/relevance review packets for a saved recommendation, a KB answer, and an X semantic alert.
tickets.scope: A small shared review-record contract and public export/record/reopen journey for one bounded example of each result type; no automatic judgments or new evaluation platform.
criteria: Packets identify exact reviewed membership, result/support IDs, methods/model versions, source spans/dates, and source-permitted original text with pending translation/reviewer fields.
Recorded judgments require actual reviewer/translator/method attribution, supported/unsupported/ambiguous/not-assessable labels, material errors/corrections, and explicit denominators.
The recorder rechecks support on export/record/read and excludes unavailable evidence rather than counting copied text toward a pass.
Technical correctness, translation-assisted labels, Japanese-original validation, and marketer usefulness remain separate statuses; missing human inputs remain pending.
Existing same-corpus monitoring/campaign review records and their semantics remain compatible or have a deliberate migration.
Integration tests prove packets do not fabricate times, translations, usefulness, source truth, or original-language accuracy; the software ticket alone establishes no human quality pass.

tickets.title: Conduct one attributable operational marketer review
tickets.what: A named human reviewer completes one bounded evaluation of the operational campaign, assistant-enrichment, and X-alert journeys with recorded evidence and limitations.
tickets.scope: A validation activity using implemented review tools and a fixed permitted corpus/window selection; no code feature, invented benchmark, or generalized accuracy/sales claim.
criteria: Select exact permitted reviewed examples and record reviewer identity/time, prior exposure, task order, and corpus/window membership before making a quality claim.

Capture actual manual baseline inputs and observed assisted task times/inspected evidence where the existing procedure requires them, plus a useful finding and reusable candidate decision or deliberate deferral.
Record actual feedback for campaign rank/rationale, assistant gaps/approval/publication behavior, and quantitative/semantic alert interpretation using the prepared packets.
Material unsupported claims, translation errors, or usability failures are documented with corrections or follow-up defects; they cannot be hidden to manufacture a pass.
Language and usefulness conclusions retain their actual denominators and qualifications; Japanese-original accuracy stays unvalidated without qualified original-language adjudication.

A named reviewer and permitted examples are explicit external prerequisites. If unavailable, keep the review pending and do not mark this validation ticket complete or replace the reviewer with model output.
